name: Bob Dylan
hook: Nobel laureate, folk-rock pioneer, and the voice behind a dozen songbook standards.

facts.label: Robert Zimmerman
facts.statement: Bob Dylan was born Robert Zimmerman and grew up in Hibbing, Minnesota, on the Mesabi Range.

facts.label: "Blowin' in the Wind"
facts.statement: "Blowin' in the Wind" is his early anthem, a No. 2 hit for Peter, Paul and Mary, asking how many seas a white dove must sail.

facts.label: "Mr. Tambourine Man"
facts.statement: He wrote "Mr. Tambourine Man"; The Byrds' 1965 cover flew to No. 1 and helped launch folk rock.

facts.label: "All Along the Watchtower"
facts.statement: Jimi Hendrix's cover of his "All Along the Watchtower" topped a Rolling Stone poll of greatest covers; Dylan called it overwhelming.

facts.label: Nobel Prize
facts.statement: Dylan won the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature; he and George Bernard Shaw are the only people with both a Nobel in Literature and an Oscar.

facts.label: the Traveling Wilburys
facts.statement: In 1988 he joined George Harrison, Jeff Lynne, Roy Orbison and Tom Petty in the Traveling Wilburys, whose hit was "Handle with Care."

facts.label: harmonica
facts.statement: Dylan is famous for the harmonica, or mouth organ; Hohner makes a Bob Dylan signature model.
